setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "db-query-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for db-query skill evals"

evals.name: composed-predicate-query
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a storage component eval_carrier_rule_storage (package Utilities) with columns carrier_id (number), service_level (string), region (string), and is_active (boolean) — all optional. Then create a function eval_find_carrier_rules_flow that takes carrier_id (number), regions (string[]), and include_unset_active (boolean), and returns the matching rules: rows where carrier_id equals the input AND region is one of the given regions AND (is_active is true OR — only when include_unset_active is true — is_active has never been set). Return out-params match_count (number) and service_levels (string[]).
evals.expected_output: A storage plus a validated/upserted function whose $db predicate composes .equals/.in/.isNull with .and/.or inside a single .where callback, ends in .toList(), and treats result-row fields as TypeScript-optional.
expectations: The transcript creates the storage component (eval_carrier_rule_storage) before or alongside the function, and the function accesses it via $db.Utilities.eval_carrier_rule_storage
The predicate composes conditions with the fluent .and(...) / .or(...) methods on column expressions — it does NOT use native &&, ||, ===, or !== inside the .where callback
The predicate uses .equals(...) for the carrier_id comparison and .in([...]) (or .in(regions)) for the region set membership
The is_active never-set branch uses .isNull() (composed via .or with .equals(true)), not a comparison against null with === or .equals(null)
The code contains none of the non-existent operator names .notEquals, .greaterThan, .greaterThanOrEqual, .ge, or .le anywhere in the $db predicate
The .where(...) chain ends in a terminal .toList() (the cursor is materialized, not left dangling)
Result rows are treated as TypeScript-optional: no strict local row type annotation (e.g. no 'id: string' / non-optional fields), and field access on rows uses ?. / ?? / $utils.isDefined narrowing
The transcript contains 'dxs function validate' and 'dxs configuration upsert flow' for the function (round-trip owned by function-creator)

evals.name: required-column-read-then-patch
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a storage component eval_carton_spec_storage (package Utilities) with columns spec_code (string, required), max_weight (number, required), and notes (string, optional). Then create a function eval_update_carton_max_weight_flow that takes spec_id (string) and new_max_weight (number), updates that record's max_weight, and returns an out-param success (boolean).
evals.expected_output: A function whose .update(id, patch) call passes the id string directly and — because the storage has required:true columns — reads the current row first and echoes every required column in the patch.
expectations: The .update call passes the id string directly as the first argument — .update(specId, { ... }) — NOT a predicate callback like .update(r => r.id.equals(specId), ...)
Before patching, the code reads the current row (a .where(r => r.id.equals(...)) ... .toList() or equivalent fetch) — the read-then-patch idiom for storages with required: true columns
The patch object echoes every required: true column: it includes spec_code (unchanged, copied from the read row) alongside the new max_weight — not a max_weight-only patch
The read result is guarded before indexing: the materialized list is coalesced (?? []) or the row is checked with $utils.isDefined / an explicit undefined check before the patch runs
The lookup predicate uses the fluent .equals(...) operator, not ===
The transcript contains 'dxs function validate' and 'dxs configuration upsert flow' for the function

evals.name: add-returns-id-string
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: using the storage eval_carton_spec_storage (create it first if it does not exist on the branch: spec_code string required, max_weight number required, notes string optional), create a function eval_create_carton_spec_flow that takes spec_code (string), max_weight (number), and notes (string), inserts a new spec row via $db, and returns the generated record id as out-param new_spec_id (string).
evals.expected_output: A function whose .add(record) return value is treated as the generated id string itself — assigned directly to the out-param, never dereferenced as a record.
expectations: The code treats the .add(...) return value as the generated id STRING: the awaited return is assigned (directly or via a local) to $flow.outParams.new_spec_id

The code does NOT dereference an id property on the .add return value — no added.id, added?.id, or (await ...add(...)).id anywhere (that fails the TS pass with "Property 'id' does not exist on type 'string'")
The out-param new_spec_id is declared as type string
The inserted record's field names match the storage's snake_case column ids exactly (spec_code, max_weight, notes)
The transcript contains 'dxs function validate' and 'dxs configuration upsert flow' for the function

evals.name: tolist-coalesce-on-fresh-storage
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a brand-new storage component eval_dock_event_storage (package Utilities) with columns event_code (string), dock_door (string), and occurred_on (date) — all optional. Then create a function eval_get_latest_dock_event_flow that takes dock_door (string) and returns latest_event_code (string) and event_count (number): the event_code of the most recent matching row (by occurred_on descending) and the total number of matching rows. This storage will have never been written to when the function first runs in a fresh environment — the function must not throw in that case.
evals.expected_output: A function whose .toList() result is coalesced to an empty array before any indexing or .length access, per the undefined-on-fresh-storage rule.
expectations: The materialized list is coalesced before use: the code wraps the read as (await $db....toList()) ?? [] (or an equivalent explicit undefined-check on the ARRAY) before any [0] indexing or .length access
The code does NOT rely solely on optional-chaining the row (rows[0]?.event_code) without first coalescing the array — the [0] index itself throws on a fresh storage where .toList() returns undefined
The query uses the fluent .equals(...) for the dock_door filter and a .sort({ occurred_on: 'desc' }) (or equivalent fluent sort) with a terminal .toList()
The out-params are populated with optional-narrowing on row fields (?? fallback or $utils.isDefined), since $db result fields are TypeScript-optional
event_count is derived from the coalesced array's .length (or an equivalently guarded count) so it is 0, not a crash, on a never-written storage
The transcript contains 'dxs function validate' and 'dxs configuration upsert flow' for the function
